patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` updates the exact `stream == NULL` unterminated-enclosure cleanup in `php_fgetcsv()`. On the original PoC, the vulnerable trace reaches `cleanup_guard` with `hunk_begin_before == bptr_before`, leaves `hunk_begin_after > bptr_after`, then reaches the protected `final_copy` event and crashes with AddressSanitizer `negative-size-param`. The fixed trace reaches the same `cleanup_guard` and `final_copy` events, but the added `if (hunk_begin == bptr) --hunk_begin;` step backtracks `hunk_begin` before `--bptr`, so `hunk_begin_after == bptr_after` and the final copy executes cleanly.

nodes.description: First project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled PHP string and CSV control characters into vulnerability-relevant parser state. The staged script reaches `str_getcsv("\xFF", "", "\xFF", "\x00")`, so this call forwards the exact one-byte data buffer, enclosure byte `0xFF`, and escape byte `0x00` into `php_fgetcsv`.

Root cause fixed by the patch. In the `stream == NULL` unterminated-enclosure cleanup, vulnerable code only retreats `bptr` when parsing has advanced past `limit`; it omits the added `if (hunk_begin == bptr) --hunk_begin;` obligation, so the witness can leave `hunk_begin > bptr` and make the later copy length negative.
Crash sink. The vulnerable cleanup leaves `hunk_begin` one byte ahead of `bptr`, so this final field copy computes size `-1` and reaches the saved AddressSanitizer `negative-size-param` report.
